# Retail Store Daily Checklist: Opening, Closing & More

Success in business is rarely the result of a single action, but rather the result of many small actions performed consistently. There are a number of tasks that need to be performed in your retail store every day to keep it humming and on track—so you can enjoy a stronger and more profitable business.


The easiest way to make sure these get done regularly and on time is with a retail store daily checklist. Let’s dive into what these are and what they should include.

- Why do retailers need a daily checklist?
- Who’s responsible for completing tasks on the checklist?
- What should you include in an opening checklist?
- What should you check during the day and at closing?

## What is a retail store daily checklist?


A retail store daily checklist is a structured list of recurring tasks that need to be performed every day to keep operations consistent, boost staff efficiency and maintain a welcoming shopping environment.


To keep daily routines manageable, these checklists are typically split into three distinct shifts:


- **Opening checklist** : Covers essential setup tasks like booting up POS systems, setting cash floats, checking safety hazards and prepping displays before doors open.
- **Mid-day checklist** : Focuses on maintaining store standards during business hours, including shelf facing, fitting room sweeps, restocking and order fulfillment.
- **Closing checklist** : Guides end-of-day procedures such as cash reconciliation, sales reporting, securing the premises and prepping the store for the next day.


Systematically following these everyday retail store daily checklists ensures high operational standards and a seamless customer experience from first shift to lights out.


## Why do retailers need an everyday retail store daily checklist?


A retail daily task list ensures that tasks are performed consistently, regardless of who’s working. By standardizing daily tasks, your team knows exactly what’s expected of them and when, helping to ensure a uniform customer experience that helps maintain your brand integrity.


But that’s just one benefit. A retail store daily checklist can upgrade your operations across the board, from sales to security, by:


- Streamlining daily operations by providing a clear outline of tasks.
- Helping employees prioritize their work, leading to increased productivity.
- Helping new employees learn the ropes, understand what’s expected of them and become productive more quickly.
- Increasing accountability and making it easier for managers to identify performance issues.
- Optimizing store layout and product placement for better sales performance.
- Enhancing the shopping experience by ensuring the store is well-maintained and well-stocked, leading to higher customer satisfaction and loyalty.
- Ensuring that safety protocols are consistently followed, lowering the risk of theft or robbery.
- Reducing the risk of health & safety violations and accidents.


## Who’s responsible for completing tasks on the daily checklist?


Who’s responsible for actually doing the tasks on a retail store daily operations checklist? Well the TL;DR is that it depends on the task.


While many of the items on opening, mid-day and closing store checklists will be completed by store managers—especially tasks like counting cash and preparing cash deposits, reconciling sales in the[point of sale system](https://www.lightspeedhq.com/pos/) , running sales reports, setting the alarm system, etc.—a lot of them can be completed by sales associates and cashiers. Completing the retail store daily task list is the responsibility of the entire staff.


## What should you include in a retail store opening checklist?


Your retail store opening checklist should be tailored to your specific store, operations and procedures, but here’s an example of what could be included.


### Sample retail opening checklist


#### Security


Before you enter the store, always do a perimeter check. Check for broken windows and other signs of a break-in. If you see any signs of a break-in, do not enter the store. Call the police from a safe distance.


#### Housekeeping


Make sure your store is clean and presentable before customers start coming in.


- Make sure windows are clean and streak-free.
- Make sure fitting rooms and common areas are neat and tidy.
- Check for potential safety hazards (tripping hazards, spills on the floor, stuff hanging from the ceiling, etc.) and make sure they’re gone before you open.
- Ensure restrooms are clean and stocked with necessary supplies.
- Do a quick sweep of the shop floor to clear dirt and dust.
- Don’t forget your storefront/entrance—give it a quick sweep and clear any ice or snow away in winter.


#### Electronics


Turn on lights, electronics and appliances. For example:


- lights and electronic displays
- point of sale (POS) system
- HVAC system
- TV and sound system
- computers, tablets and other gadgets


You can wait until right before you open for some of these—but you’ll probably at least want some lights on while you’re going through your opening checklist. (And maybe some music.)


#### POS/Cash registers


Before you open your doors, prep your[cash registers](https://www.lightspeedhq.com/blog/cash-register-systems/) for the day so your team is ready to sell.


- Launch your POS software
- Do a quick POS security check (check for signs of tampering)*
- Make sure the previous day was properly closed out
- Run your inventory and sales reports
- Prep your cash float for each cash drawer
- Enter your daily cash float in your POS
- Restock receipt paper and check barcode scanners


**POS fraud is an unfortunate reality in retail, whether you’re a mom-and-pop store or a million-dollar franchise. An[iPad POS system](https://www.lightspeedhq.com/ipad-point-of-sale/) such as Lightspeed’s can help you leverage Apple’s market-leading privacy and security features to protect your business from POS fraud.*


#### Merchandising


[Visual merchandising and product displays](https://www.lightspeedhq.com/blog/visual-merchandising/) have a direct influence on your sales, so you want to make sure products are presented in the best way possible every day before you open.


- Make sure shelves and product displays are clean and organized.
- Give shelves a quick dust if necessary, and remove anything that shouldn’t be there (e.g. customers’ discarded coffee cups).
- Make sure your window displays look right—because you never know (seriously,[you never know](https://www.yahoo.com/news/man-posed-mannequin-shop-window-061321100.html?guccounter=1&guce_referrer=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZ29vZ2xlLmNvbS8&guce_referrer_sig=AQAAAL2qPglqczlo27F2d4qLhmgyhSaa5RxQBHLK9imIZmnPIVxtkxO8dyRqOODkCo8nTrD-qH8_R9fgQprzTE9oNlIqZFY6GjWe4hQh-iZBAPRJ9_2MsNAzH38SfXTuhI2kIzKO15Y2_rEnnv4JUI27WvlvD9lXTnyxqOS5kV7LD4-d) ).
- Put any products that have been discarded willy-nilly back in their proper place, regroup apparel by size if they’ve gotten all mixed up.
- Make sure your[point of purchase displays](https://www.lightspeedhq.com/blog/point-of-sale-marketing/) are fully-stocked and looking good.
- Verify stock levels for popular products.
- Restock shelves and displays as needed (especially displays which can look “off” when products are missing).
- Ensure that all signage is correct, in good condition and in its proper place.
- Make sure your refund policy is posted and visible.
- Verify that product tags are in order—prices are clearly marked, sale items are labeled, etc.


#### Staff


Great, your staff is starting to trickle in! It’s time to round up your team for a quick pre-shift meeting.


- Communicate sales targets and goals. Coach sales reps on[sales techniques](https://www.lightspeedhq.com/blog/suggestive-selling/) .
- Make sure everyone is up-to-date on your current sales and promotions.
- Review shift duties—who’s in charge of what, who is stationed where, etc.
- Discuss anything that went wrong the previous day and how it could be handled differently
- Celebrate what’s going well and where your team is excelling. Giving praise where it’s due is a great way to motivate your people.
- Review store policies if necessary. For example: “Just a quick reminder that we need to be wearing all-black no-slip shoes as per our company dress policy, *Brenda* .”


## What should you check during the day and at closing time?


Getting your store ready before opening sets you up for a good day, but maintaining mid-day momentum and a thorough end-of-day shutdown are just as critical to your success.


As always, the tasks on your mid-day and closing checklists will depend on your specific business, but there’s a good chance these should be on them.


### Sample checklist: Mid-day operations & maintenance


- Keep an eye on inventory levels and restock as needed.
- Pull products forward to be flush with the front of the shelf (known as facing, blocking or fronting).
- Complete regular safety walks through the store to check for hazards or spills.
- Keep aisles, fitting rooms and other customer touchpoints clean.
- Return unpurchased items at checkout and fitting rooms to the sales floor.
- Process new inventory deliveries and get them onto the sales floor.
- Charge mobile POS tablets and barcode scanners during quiet lulls.
- Process new online orders and prepare them for pickup.
- Record damaged, missing or defective products.
- Monitor cash handling and checkout activity.


Most of the tasks on this list will become second nature to your staff over time, but it’s good to keep a list of ‘during business hours’ tasks for training and accountability purposes.


### Sample retail store closing checklist


- Vacuum or sweep high-traffic aisles, entrance mats and fitting room floors.
- Empty all trash cans and recycling bins throughout the shop and breakroom.
- Gather abandoned items and return them to their proper locations on the sales floor.
- Clear, clean and organize all fitting rooms and customer counter space.
- Reconcile cash drawers and balance the daily register floats.
- Run final sales, register and batch reports in your POS system.
- Secure cash floats and daily cash deposits in the store safe.
- Place mobile POS tablets, barcode scanners and card readers on chargers.
- Power down non-essential lighting, displays, TVs and audio equipment.
- Double-check that all remaining customers have exited the store.
- Lock back doors, secure stockrooms and lock display cases.
- Lock main doors, set the security alarm and verify all exterior locks on departure.


A thorough closing procedure ensures your store stays secure overnight; protects your cash and inventory; and sets up your team up for a quick, stress-free opening the next day.

## Retail store daily checklist FAQs


### What should be checked before closing a retail store?


Before closing a retail store, staff need to clean and tidy up customer-facing areas, reconcile cash drawers and sales reports, secure any cash or valuables on site, lock all entry points, power down unnecessary equipment and set the security alarm. Finishing these end-of-day tasks ensures your store stays secure overnight and is ready for effortless opening the next morning.


### How often should a retail store daily checklist be updated?


A retail store daily operations checklist should be reviewed quarterly and updated whenever store operations, your tech stack or seasonal promotions change. Regularly auditing your daily task lists ensures your workflows align with current store goals, staff roles and processes.


### How can technology help manage retail store checklists?


Modern retail technology, such as cloud-based point-of-sale (POS) systems and task management apps, automates many store routines, such as cash register reconciliation, inventory tracking and sales reporting. Digital checklists allow managers to assign tasks in real time, track completion across shifts and maintain operational consistency across multiple store locations.


### What are some common daily tasks in a retail store?


Common daily retail tasks include verifying cash floats, conducting cycle counts, restocking sales displays, maintaining floor cleanliness, performing security checks and holding pre-shift staff huddles. Completing these routines helps store teams improve operational efficiency, prevent inventory shrinkage and provide a consistent customer experience.
